exercises.prompt: Identify an object that undergoes uniform circular motion. Describe how you could trace the simple harmonic motion of this object as a wave.

answer.solution: A record player undergoes uniform circular motion. You could attach dowel rod to one point on the outside edge of the turntable and attach a pen to the other end of the dowel. As the record player turns, the pen will move. You can drag a long piece of paper under the pen, capturing its motion as a wave.

exercises.prompt: (a) What is the maximum velocity of an 85.0-kg person bouncing on a bathroom scale having a force constant of $1.50 \times 10^{6}\ \text{N/m}$, if the amplitude of the bounce is 0.200 cm? (b) What is the maximum energy stored in the spring?

parts.hint: Use $\kvmax = \kX\sqrt{\kk/m}$ with the amplitude in meters.
At the turning point all the energy is in the spring, $\tfrac{1}{2}\kk\kX^2$.

exercises.prompt: At what positions is the speed of a simple harmonic oscillator half its maximum? That is, what values of $\kx/\kX$ give $\kv = \pm\kvmax/2$, where $\kX$ is the amplitude of the motion?

answer.hint: Set $\sqrt{1 - \kx^2/\kX^2} = 1/2$ and solve for $\kx/\kX$. There are two positions, one on each side of equilibrium; give the positive one.
